sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Gold's structural rally, driven by central-bank buying and geopolitical hedging, continues to lift Indonesian gold miners like BRMS and AMMN, with upside persisting as real rates stay elevated.
Indonesia's nickel downstreaming policy, including export bans and HPAL plant expansions, creates durable pricing power for integrated players like MBMA, insulating them from global ore price swings.
Coal's rally is cyclical, not structural, as thermal demand peaks in Asia and ESG capital constraints cap long-term valuations, making COAL and PSAB tactical trades rather than core holdings.
sectors.ai: Buy selectively into gold and nickel names (BRMS, AMMN, MBMA) on the back of record bullion prices and Indonesia's downstream nickel premium; take profits on coal (COAL, PSAB) as the rally looks overheated. Watch for Q3 earnings confirmation and rupiah stability before adding exposure.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's EV supply chain is structurally underpinned by nickel dominance and downstreaming mandates, making VKTR and TOBA prime beneficiaries of accelerating domestic adoption and export growth.
US utility resilience is driven by irreplaceable grid infrastructure demand from AI data centers and electrification, favoring PCG, EIX, and SRE with stable regulated returns.
Climate-tech divergence favors issuers with integrated renewable-plus-storage models (ESSA, CDIA) over pure-play volatility, as energy security and baseload reliability become investment priorities.
sectors.ai: Buy the dip in Indonesian EV/battery names (VKTR, TOBA) and resilient US utilities (PCG, EIX, SRE) on rate-cut tailwinds and domestic demand; rotate out of laggards with weak cash flow. Expect continued outperformance in ID-driven climate plays as policy support and electrification accelerate, while US names benefit from grid modernization and data-center load.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rupiah stability and falling imported input costs are widening gross margins for local FMCG players, making domestic-demand names structurally more profitable than exporters.
Government social-spending programs and Ramadan-led consumption are creating a durable mid-year demand tailwind for staple and discretionary FMCG categories.
Consolidation in Indonesia's fragmented retail channel favors scaled distributors and brand owners, driving market-share gains for listed mid-caps over smaller unlisted rivals.
sectors.ai: Indonesia consumer/FMCG is a selective long: buy domestically-exposed names with pricing power (BRRC, COIN, JARR) as ID outperformance (+1.68%) vs US (-1.06%) confirms local demand resilience; avoid palm/commodity-linked laggards (BWPT, PGUN) despite bounce. Accumulate on dips toward 1H25, targeting mid-cap staples with distribution expansion; trim any US-exposed FMCG.
